title: French Onion Soup
subtitle: Rich, deeply caramelised onion soup with a cheesy crust
excerpt: The onions need a full hour in the pan to turn properly golden and sweet. Do not rush this step. The rest of the soup comes together quickly, and the result is a bowl that needs nothing else alongside it.
sourceNotes: French onion soup is a Parisian bistro classic with roots in eighteenth-century cooking. The version with a bread and cheese crust became widely known through Les Halles, the former Paris market district.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the soup without the bread topping. Reheat and add fresh toasted bread and cheese just before serving.
recipe.batchNotes: The soup base doubles well. Portion and freeze for up to 3 months.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The soup base can be made 2 days ahead and refrigerated. Reheat before adding the topping.
recipe.temperatureNote: Grill setting for the cheese crust at the end

content.text: The onions must be a deep amber colour before you add the liquid. Pale onions give a bland, sweet soup rather than the deep savoury broth this dish is known for.
Melt the butter in a large stockpot over a medium-low heat.
Add the onions and a good pinch of salt. Stir to coat.
Cook over a low heat for 50 to 60 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes. The onions should turn deep golden brown. Scrape the bottom of the pan each time.
Add the flour. Stir and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the vinegar. Stir to deglaze any stuck bits.
Add the stock, bay leaves, and thyme. Bring to a simmer.
Simmer for 10 minutes. Remove the bay leaves and thyme stalks. Season well.
Heat the grill to high. Toast 4 thick slices of bread on the baking tray until golden.
Ladle the soup into 4 heatproof bowls. Place a toast slice on top of each.
Pile the grated cheese on top of each toast. Place under the grill for 2 to 3 minutes until bubbling and golden.

items.symptom: Soup tastes thin and sweet rather than rich.
items.cause: Onions were not caramelised deeply enough.
items.fix: Cook longer. The onions must be dark amber, not pale gold.

items.symptom: Onions catch and burn on the bottom.
items.cause: Heat too high or not enough stirring.
items.fix: Lower the heat and scrape the pan every few minutes.

items.symptom: Cheese does not melt evenly under the grill.
items.cause: Cheese piled too thick in one spot.
items.fix: Spread the cheese in an even layer across the whole toast.
